territorial_scope.description: Adopted by the EU Commission and addressed to Member States; covers personal data transferred from the Union to US organisations included in the Data Privacy Framework List.

evidence.quote: the United States ensures an adequate level of protection for personal data transferred from the Union to organisations in the United States

summary.short: Adequacy decision under GDPR Art. 45(3) finding that the United States ensures adequate protection for personal data transferred from the EU to US organisations on the Data Privacy Framework List, so such transfers need no further authorisation; the Commission and Member States must monitor it.
summary.long: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2023/1795 under Article 45(3) of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 finds that the United States ensures an adequate level of protection for personal data transferred from the Union to organisations in the United States that are included in the Data Privacy Framework List. Such transfers may take place without further authorisation. Eligibility rests on certification to the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework Principles (Annex I), administered by the U.S. Department of Commerce, with enforcement by the FTC or DoT. Certified organisations must provide notice, honour access and choice rights, apply onward-transfer contracts, and maintain recourse mechanisms including binding arbitration. The decision also assesses U.S. government access limits for criminal law enforcement and national security, including the safeguards of Executive Order 14086 and the Data Protection Review Court. Member States must inform the Commission of relevant cases (Art. 2), and the Commission must continuously monitor the framework and evaluate it after one year from notification (Art. 3). Annexes referenced in the text are not part of the fetched document.

notes: This part covers recitals (1) to (87) only; Articles 1 to 3 and recitals (88) onward belong to other parts, although the supplied text includes them. Empty strings replace null for registry IDs, LEI and ticker, as the schema requires strings. Recital (68) refers to 'Annex I of Annex I to this Decision', which appears to be a drafting error. Part 2 of 3 covers the end of Article 4, the recital footnotes, Annex I (Principles), the Annex I arbitral model and the Annex II transmittal letter. Empty target_instrument_id and lei/ticker fields mean no registry ID or verified identifier is available in the document. Legal basis of the Decision itself (Article 45 GDPR) is in part 1. Internal inconsistency: Annex I, Section III.11.g.iii says removal follows 30 days' notice, while footnote (17) says the Department will set a response time which will necessarily be less than 30 days. The letters from the FTC, DOT, ODNI and DOJ are listed as enclosures in Annex II; their content is not in this part. Part 3 of 3 covers Annexes III to VIII: letters from Commerce, FTC, DOT, DOJ and ODNI, footnotes, Appendix A and the abbreviations list. Empty target_instrument_id and lei/ticker values mean no registry ID or verified identifier was available. Several quotes reproduce OCR errors in the source (e.g., ofFISA, Communjty, ex officio,refer); quotes are verbatim. Appendix A lists 68 FTC matters; only the three named in the text are coded as entities. Annex III footnote 2 gives an illustrative 45-day expectation for re-certification issues, introduced by 'e.g.'.
